record.longDescription: Master of Business Administration In Human Resource Management (MBA - HRM) The Human Resource Management (HRM) course provides students with the essential knowledge and skills to manage an organization's workforce effectively. Topics include talent acquisition, employee development, performance management, and strategic HR practices. The program equips students to address contemporary HR challenges and contribute to organizational success.
record.courseDetails: Course Details The MBA in Human Resource Management course explores key concepts and practices for managing an organization’s most valuable asset—its people. Topics covered include recruitment and selection, employee training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, labor relations, and HR strategy. The course emphasizes legal and ethical considerations in HR practices and the role of HR in driving organizational culture and change. Students will also gain insights into the use of technology in HR, such as HR information systems (HRIS). Practical case studies and real-world applications will help students develop critical problem-solving and decision-making skills. Upon completion, students will be prepared to lead HR initiatives that align with organizational goals and drive overall performance. After the successful completion of this course, you will understand the following: Analyze how socioeconomic and legal factors impact business operations and decision-making. Understand fundamental accounting and finance principles to interpret financial statements and assess organizational performance. Apply marketing concepts and strategies to effectively reach and engage target audiences. Develop skills for managing human resources to enhance employee performance and organizational culture. Formulate and evaluate business strategies that align with organizational goals and market conditions. Demonstrate the ability to make sound HR related decisions that support effective business organization and growth.
outcomes: Analyze how socioeconomic and legal factors impact business operations and decision-making.
Understand fundamental accounting and finance principles to interpret financial statements and assess organizational performance.
Apply marketing concepts and strategies to effectively reach and engage target audiences.
Develop skills for managing human resources to enhance employee performance and organizational culture.
Formulate and evaluate business strategies that align with organizational goals and market conditions.
Demonstrate the ability to make sound HR related decisions that support effective business organization and growth.

modules.title: Socioeconomic And Legal Environment
modules.summary: The "Socioeconomic and Legal Environment" course examines the key social, economic, and legal factors that influence business practices and organizational decision-making. It covers the impact of socioeconomic trends, such as income distribution, labor markets, and globalization, on business operations and strategy. The course also delves into the legal frameworks governing business activities, including contracts, labor laws, corporate governance, intellectual property, and environmental regulations. Students will analyze how businesses navigate these external forces to ensure compliance, mitigate risks, and create sustainable value. Through case studies and practical insights, the course prepares students to understand and adapt to a complex, dynamic business environment.

modules.title: Accounting And Finance
modules.summary: The "Accounting and Finance" course provides a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices in both fields, essential for effective business management. Students will explore financial accounting, management accounting, and financial reporting, learning how to prepare, analyze, and interpret financial statements. The course also covers key financial management topics, including budgeting, financial planning, investment analysis, and risk management. Emphasis is placed on using accounting and financial data to make informed decisions, optimize resource allocation, and ensure organizational financial health. Through real-world examples and case studies, students will gain practical skills in analyzing financial performance and implementing sound financial strategies.

Master of Business Administration In Human Resource Management (MBA - HRM) The Human Resource Management (HRM) course provides students with the essential knowledge and skills to manage an organization's workforce effectively. Topics include talent acquisition, employee development, performance management, and strategic HR practices. The program equips students to address contemporary HR challenges and contribute to organizational success.
Course Details

The MBA in Human Resource Management course explores key concepts and practices for managing an organization’s most valuable asset—its people. Topics covered include recruitment and selection, employee training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, labor relations, and HR strategy. The course emphasizes legal and ethical considerations in HR practices and the role of HR in driving organizational culture and change. Students will also gain insights into the use of technology in HR, such as HR information systems (HRIS). Practical case studies and real-world applications will help students develop critical problem-solving and decision-making skills. Upon completion, students will be prepared to lead HR initiatives that align with organizational goals and drive overall performance.

blocks.text:
Socioeconomic And Legal Environment
The "Socioeconomic and Legal Environment" course examines the key social, economic, and legal factors that influence business practices and organizational decision-making. It covers the impact of socioeconomic trends, such as income distribution, labor markets, and globalization, on business operations and strategy. The course also delves into the legal frameworks governing business activities, including contracts, labor laws, corporate governance, intellectual property, and environmental regulations. Students will analyze how businesses navigate these external forces to ensure compliance, mitigate risks, and create sustainable value. Through case studies and practical insights, the course prepares students to understand and adapt to a complex, dynamic business environment.

Master of Business Administration In Human Resource Management (MBA - HRM)

Master of Business Administration In Human Resource Management (MBA - HRM) The Human Resource Management (HRM) course provides students with the essential knowledge and skills to manage an organization's workforce effectively. Topics include talent acquisition, employee development, performance management, and strategic HR practices. The program equips students to address contemporary HR challenges and contribute to organizational success.
Course Details

The MBA in Human Resource Management course explores key concepts and practices for managing an organization’s most valuable asset—its people. Topics covered include recruitment and selection, employee training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, labor relations, and HR strategy. The course emphasizes legal and ethical considerations in HR practices and the role of HR in driving organizational culture and change. Students will also gain insights into the use of technology in HR, such as HR information systems (HRIS). Practical case studies and real-world applications will help students develop critical problem-solving and decision-making skills. Upon completion, students will be prepared to lead HR initiatives that align with organizational goals and drive overall performance.

modules.title: Socioeconomic And Legal Environment
modules.summary: The "Socioeconomic and Legal Environment" course examines the key social, economic, and legal factors that influence business practices and organizational decision-making. It covers the impact of socioeconomic trends, such as income distribution, labor markets, and globalization, on business operations and strategy. The course also delves into the legal frameworks governing business activities, including contracts, labor laws, corporate governance, intellectual property, and environmental regulations. Students will analyze how businesses navigate these external forces to ensure compliance, mitigate risks, and create sustainable value. Through case studies and practical insights, the course prepares students to understand and adapt to a complex, dynamic business environment.

modules.summary: The "Accounting and Finance" course provides a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices in both fields, essential for effective business management. Students will explore financial accounting, management accounting, and financial reporting, learning how to prepare, analyze, and interpret financial statements. The course also covers key financial management topics, including budgeting, financial planning, investment analysis, and risk management. Emphasis is placed on using accounting and financial data to make informed decisions, optimize resource allocation, and ensure organizational financial health. Through real-world examples and case studies, students will gain practical skills in analyzing financial performance and implementing sound financial strategies.

evidence.heading: courseDetails
evidence.text:
Course Details
The MBA in Human Resource Management course explores key concepts and practices for managing an organization’s most valuable asset—its people. Topics covered include recruitment and selection, employee training and development, performance management, compensation and benefits, labor relations, and HR strategy. The course emphasizes legal and ethical considerations in HR practices and the role of HR in driving organizational culture and change. Students will also gain insights into the use of technology in HR, such as HR information systems (HRIS). Practical case studies and real-world applications will help students develop critical problem-solving and decision-making skills. Upon completion, students will be prepared to lead HR initiatives that align with organizational goals and drive overall performance.

Upon completion, students will be prepared to lead HR initiatives that align with organizational goals and drive overall performance. After the successful completion of this course, you will understand the following: Analyze how socioeconomic and legal factors impact business operations and decision-making. Understand fundamental accounting and finance principles to interpret financial statements and assess organizational performance. Apply marketing concepts and strategies to effectively reach and engage target audiences. Develop skills for managing human resources to enhance employee performance and organizational culture. Formulate and evaluate business strategies that align with organizational goals and market conditions. Demonstrate the ability to make sound HR related decisions that support effective business organization and growth.

The "Accounting and Finance" course provides a comprehensive understanding of the principles and practices in both fields, essential for effective business management. Students will explore financial accounting, management accounting, and financial reporting, learning how to prepare, analyze, and interpret financial statements. The course also covers key financial management topics, including budgeting, financial planning, investment analysis, and risk management. Emphasis is placed on using accounting and financial data to make informed decisions, optimize resource allocation, and ensure organizational financial health. Through real-world examples and case studies, students will gain practical skills in analyzing financial performance and implementing sound financial strategies.
